sources.author: Vladan Majerech
sources.title: 100 prisoners and a lightbulb – looking back

titleEvidence.locator: Fixed arXiv v1 PDF page 1, first title line; abstract page title preserves an ASCII double-hyphen variant, recorded separately in evidence.

supports: Section 1 distinguishes known initial switch state with unknown visit count (nB2) from versions with shared visit counts or unknown initial state.

Section 3 describes nB2 single-collector signaling: an unsent non-collector leaves ON unchanged and retains its contribution; on OFF it sends once by switching ON. Only the collector collects by switching OFF.
The collector gathers n−1 distinct non-collector contributions. Its paper counter starts at 1−n and ends at 0; the episode uses the equivalent shifted counter from 0 to n−1.
sources.sections: Full 12-page extracted PDF text read; the episode specifically uses §1 and the opening nB2 construction in §3, PDF pages 1–3. Later random-scheduling optimizations, simulation averages and figures are not episode results.

quotation.text: Before the game starts one prisoner should be chosen to be a collector.
quotation.locator: §3 Communication terminology, PDF page 2, paragraph after the non-collector ON/OFF rule.

verification.method: Actually opened the fixed v1 PDF through the purpose-built web tool and read extracted text covering all 12 pages; separately read the arXiv abstract page for explicit author and submission date. Original title and author are from the PDF first page. No actual PDF-figure visual inspection, source-code reproduction or simulation reproduction claim.

sources.note: This 2022 primary-author paper supplies current protocol context in addition to the historical reference. Its larger optimization problem uses stronger visit-count/random-selection assumptions; those are not added to this episode. Virtual tokens are explanatory bookkeeping in the paper, not physical marks or an extra communication channel. The 13-word quotation supports choosing one collector, not by itself the episode’s arbitrary-fair-schedule proof.

sources.author: Hans van Ditmarsch; Jan van Eijck; William Wu
sources.title: One Hundred Prisoners and a Lightbulb — Logic and Computation

titleEvidence.locator: Original author-hosted PDF page 1, heading and the three explicit author blocks; CWI bibliographic record gives an ASCII triple-hyphen title variant.

sources.version: KR 2010; CWI publication record dated 2010-05-01; original PDF copyright year 2010. 历史仅参考。
supports: The original puzzle states an initially OFF light, no fixed interrogation order or interval, and every prisoner being selected again after any stage.
Protocol 1 assigns one counter and permits each other prisoner to switch ON only the first time that prisoner enters while the light is OFF.
The discussion of an unknown initial state explains that an initial ON could create an unearned count; the initial-OFF premise must not be silently dropped.
sources.sections: Actual extracted text on PDF pages 1–2: problem statement, Protocol 1, and discussion immediately before Protocol 3. The remaining formal epistemic-model and runtime sections were not read in this run.

quotation.text: the first time they enter the room when the light is off, they turn it on; on all other occasions, they do nothing.
quotation.locator: Protocol 1, PDF page 1, non-counting-prisoner rule after the colon.

verification.method: Actually opened the original author-hosted PDF and read extracted problem/Protocol 1/unknown-initial-state text on pages 1–2; separately read the CWI institutional publication record for its 2010-05-01 date and AAAI Press publisher. Title/three author names were checked from the actual PDF heading and author blocks, not from record ordering or copyright ownership.

sources.note: 历史仅参考，不能作为唯一主论证。The original Protocol 1 turns OFF on the first n−2 received signals and announces on the next ON observation; the episode chooses to turn OFF and increment also on the last signal before announcing. That explicit local-action variant is validated independently rather than attributed word-for-word to this paper. The 23-word quote preserves the conditional first time while OFF, not an unconditional first visit.
